cards.headline: No ko: White answers Black's capture by taking the stone at A16 instead of retaking, then captures three stones for two eyes. ALIVE, not KO−.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line. White 12 ataris Black 3 and Black 5 but is in atari itself, as is Black 7. The tree marks the leaf S[KO-]; the solver said ALIVE.

diagrams.moves: A18 A15 pass C18 pass A19
diagrams.caption: Black 13 captures the stone at A19 and puts White's left group in atari. White 14 captures the stone at A16 instead of retaking and keeps a liberty at A14, so Black cannot recapture. Black 15 and Black 17 are played elsewhere: White 16 ataris Black 13 and the stones at B19 and C19 on their shared liberty A19, where Black cannot play, and White 18 captures three for two eyes.

The bent-four try. Black 15 connects at A19, White 16 captures four stones, Black 17 takes the bent-four point, and Black 19 captures White 18, a ko. White 20 does not need the ko: Black 17 and Black 19 now both hang on A19, and Black cannot connect there while White keeps outside liberties at A16 and E19. White captures two there next and has two eyes.

Taking an outside liberty costs Black two moves. Black 15 and Black 17 capture White 14, and Black 17 ataris White's whole group, but White 16 has already put three stones in atari, and White 18 captures them first: two eyes.

text: There is no ko here. White 12 captured nothing, and Black must capture it with Black 13 in Diagram 2: any other move lets White capture the stones at B19 and C19 by playing C18, and live. White 14 is forced too: connecting at C18 instead would put White's whole group in atari at E19, and Black would capture it all. But it is enough: Black cannot stop White 16 and White 18.

The bent-four try in Diagram 3 fails because White still has outside liberties at A16 and E19, so White never has to fight the ko. Each liberty costs Black two moves to fill, as in Diagram 4, while White needs one move to settle the corner.

Even if Black 13 started a ko, Black would have taken first: KO+, never KO−. The solver says ALIVE even when Black may ignore the ko ban, and even though its narrow area favours Black: it counts A14 as Black's wall, which turns White 14's capture into a ko. Both areas give ALIVE after White 16 in Diagram 3 and after White 18 in Diagram 4. The wider area ran out of budget after White 16 in Diagram 2, where White simply captures three.
